classification_rationale: the budget read fell back to the 250 MiB default on a read error, so the pass deleted down to a smaller target than the one configured
trigger: the db_budget_bytes config read fails (store error) while a larger budget is configured
summary: configured_budget_bytes read the setting through get_config, which fails open to the default. Fixed: the read is tri-state (try_get_config, budget_from_config); an unreadable budget skips the pass, clears the catch-up latch and is retried on the next pass.

classification_rationale: the raw-tier cutoff used min(mark, now-24h) and the hourly floor ignored the daily mark, so rows not yet summarised could become evictable
trigger: a rollup mark dated in the future, or an implausibly large clock reading, reaches run_budget
summary: Eviction floors trusted a mark that could lie ahead of the clock. Fixed: the raw tier is skipped when the mark is ahead of now or implausible, and the hourly floor is bounded by the daily mark.

classification_rationale: the seen set stayed pinned to the future hour, so later real hours never cleared it and first sightings were dropped with no counter
trigger: one tick stamped in a future hour is seen before real-time ticks
summary: HourlySeenSet only cleared on a later hour. Fixed: any change of hour, earlier or later, clears the set.

policy_floor: routed-concern: C++ resource ownership and lifetime (docs/cpp-conventions.md): new code uses the shared RAII owner, not a manual sqlite3_free
classification_rationale: new code used a manual sqlite3_free where the file's own RAII owner is the required idiom; no wrong behaviour on the paths read
trigger: new code frees a SQLite error string by hand where SqliteErrMsg exists
summary: Two new sites freed err_msg manually. Fixed: both use SqliteErrMsg. Gates as a contract violation under the C++ resource-ownership routed concern, not by derivation.

classification_rationale: an all-zero StorageBytes was read as 'within budget' and budget_over_bytes published 0, presenting an unknown size as a good one
trigger: the page-count pragma read fails in storage_bytes_locked
summary: storage_bytes_locked returned zeros on failure. Fixed: StorageBytes carries ok; run_budget reports failed, enforce_budget leaves the published over-budget figure unchanged.

classification_rationale: a future marker's negative age compared less than a day, so the conversion was held off until the clock caught up
trigger: the stored conversion marker is ahead of the clock (written during a forward clock excursion)
summary: vacuum_decision treated a future marker as recent. Fixed: a marker ahead of now counts as stale.

classification_rationale: the budget floors derive from the same untrusted clock reading the retention guard just refused
trigger: the clock steps or is implausible while retention declines it; the budget pass still runs on the same reading
summary: enforce_budget ignored the retention clock verdict. Fixed: do_rollup skips the budget pass (counted as retention_guard|__budget__) when the guard declined or failed, and clears any pending catch-up.

classification_rationale: the gate waited for data to fall under target, which can never happen once eviction has nothing left to take, so the file never shrinks
trigger: eviction is exhausted while data stays above target and the freelist is large
summary: vacuum_decision skipped whenever data exceeded target. Fixed: eviction_exhausted lets the conversion run, still behind the freelist, free-disk and daily-retry gates.

classification_rationale: the plan-time ruling that the VACUUM holds the lock did not weigh that it also holds the shared trigger thread
trigger: the one-off VACUUM runs on the single interval-trigger thread with the database lock held
summary: The conversion stalls every trigger and parks status and collector writes for its duration, once per database. Dispositioned by recording the bound (duration follows the used data, free-disk gate at twice that size, attempt marker written before the run) and disclosing the stall in the operator notes; the catch-up slice uses try_lock so the fast tick does not queue behind it.

classification_rationale: the 48 h hourly floor was shorter than the two completed UTC days the agent re-sends for that source, and the server overwrites unconditionally
trigger: the budget evicts procperf hourly rows younger than the window the daily sync re-sends
summary: The procperf hourly floor was below the sync re-send window. Fixed: procperf uses a floor of at least five days; the other sources keep 48 h.

classification_rationale: the capability catalogue entry classifies the action Reversible, contradicting an irreversible delete
trigger: an operator reads echo.configure as reversible while db_budget_bytes irreversibly deletes rows inside the retention window
summary: Agent-side half fixed: the db_budget_bytes wording in the definition, README and manual states the deletion is permanent, happens before the tier limit and that raising the budget restores nothing. The catalogue classification lives in server code, outside this change, and is tracked as B11-server.

classification_rationale: a server-owned classification contradicts the agent-side wording
trigger: the echo.configure catalogue entry is Mutating, Reversible, Medium
summary: Not edited here: a server file is outside this change's agent-only scope. Rejected for this change and carried to the owner of the server catalogue for a classification ruling.

classification_rationale: the user manual, upgrade notes and implementer guide said nothing about the first-pass irreversible deletion, and the implementer guide said rows remain queryable on upgrade
trigger: an operator upgrades with rows older than the budget allows and finds no note that they will be deleted
summary: Fixed in the documentation round: an upgrade subsection in the Echo manual, a section in the upgrade notes, corrected implementer-guide rows including rollback, and the changelog split.

classification_rationale: text calling the retention depth guaranteed is no longer true once the budget can evict inside it
trigger: an operator reads the retention depth as guaranteed while the byte budget can shorten it
summary: Agent-side and documentation half fixed (the rest-api.md retention-depth sentence now states the depth holds while the device is within its byte budget). The settings-page hint string is server UI code, outside this change, and is tracked as B13-server.

classification_rationale: a server-owned UI string contradicts the byte-budget behaviour
trigger: the settings page hint describes the retention depth as guaranteed
summary: Not edited here: server UI code is outside this change's agent-only scope. Rejected for this change and carried to the owner of the settings page.

classification_rationale: no test failed when the catch-up call was removed; the behaviour was proven only by reading
trigger: the fast-tick catch-up call in collect_fast is removed or broken
summary: Coverage gap, found by two reviewers. Adapted: a deterministic aggregator-level test pins the catch-up slice and its admitted clock, instead of a wall-clock test; the run on the Windows and Linux lanes remains an obligation of the test gate. Reporter reference is unresolved (the raw review phases are run scratch, not committed).

classification_rationale: nothing discriminated commit-after-insert from commit-before-insert at plugin level
trigger: an insert fails after the closing-socket or module seen set was filtered
summary: Coverage gap on de-duplication preservation after a failed insert. Adapted: plugin-level tests added, each with a deletion experiment; the run on the Windows and Linux lanes remains an obligation of the test gate. Reporter reference is unresolved (the raw review phases are run scratch, not committed).

classification_rationale: the catch-up slice evicted on a fresh clock reading that no retention guard had admitted, contradicting the rule that every eviction runs on an admitted reading
trigger: a clock step forward between the maintenance pass that armed the catch-up latch and the next fast tick
summary: run_budget_catch_up called enforce_budget with now_epoch_seconds(). Fixed: the latch stores the clock reading the arming pass was admitted with and every slice runs with it; the next guarded maintenance pass admits or refuses a new one. A regression test covers a forward step between arming and the next slice. Reporter reference is unresolved (the raw review phases are run scratch, not committed).
